title: How do we add these pairs of expressions?
description: Six pairs of expressions are added by writing one after the other, opening the one bracket, and joining like terms. The last two pairs cancel completely and give zero.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding two expressions means joining their like terms, and the minus sign before a bracket changes the signs inside. Watch for students who miss that the last two pairs are exact opposites.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of opening a bracket and joining like terms, since the sum of two expressions is written as one long expression and then simplified.
video_script.substitution: The method of opening a bracket and joining terms, with each pair of expressions in place of the matchstick formula.
video_script.anchor: six pairs of expressions to be added
video_script.payoff_line: Every pair has now been added

final_answer.spoken: thirteen d plus c minus two; seven f plus four s minus four; two c minus d minus two; minus seven f minus four s plus three; zero; zero

maths_rules: (a) d: 4d + 9d = 13d; c: -7c + 8c = c; numbers 9 - 11 = -2; sum 13d + c - 2
video_script.design: One idea: write both expressions, open any bracket, then join like terms. Assumes the example of opening a bracket. The six pairs stay on the stage and are done one at a time.

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>It asks us to add the two expressions in each of six pairs.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>Each expression has two letters and a plain number.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>What is the sum of each pair?

beats.on_screen: the six pairs stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: to add two expressions, write one after the other ; then join the terms with the same letter

marks.g1: two expressions are written one after the other
marks.g2: terms with the same letter slide together

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>To add two expressions, we write one after the other.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Then we join the terms that have the same letter.

marks.gv1: the six pairs are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, six pairs of expressions in the letters d, c, f, s, m and n. One pair has a bracket.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum of the two expressions in each pair
narration: <bookmark mark='fd'/>We add the two expressions in every pair. We work the same way as the example in your book.

marks.s1b: the c terms and the numbers are joined

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>First, the first pair. The d terms are four d and nine d, which make thirteen d.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>The c terms are minus seven c and eight c, which make c. The numbers are nine and minus eleven, which make minus two.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>The sum is thirteen d plus c minus two.

marks.s2b: the s terms and the numbers are joined

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Second, the second pair. The f terms are minus six f and thirteen f, which make seven f.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>The s terms are minus eight s and twelve s, which make four s. The numbers are nineteen and minus twenty three, which make minus four.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>The sum is seven f plus four s minus four.

marks.s3a: the bracket is opened with both signs changed
marks.s3b: the d terms and c terms are joined
marks.s3c: the numbers are joined and the sum is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Third, the third pair has a bracket. The second expression is sixteen c minus the bracket eleven plus nine d. The minus sign changes both signs inside.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>The d terms are eight d and minus nine d, which make minus d. The c terms are minus fourteen c and sixteen c, which make two c.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>The numbers are nine and minus eleven, which make minus two. The sum is two c minus d minus two.

marks.s4c: the numbers are joined and the sum is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Fourth, the fourth pair. The f terms are six f and minus thirteen f, which make minus seven f.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>The s terms are eight s and minus twelve s, which make minus four s.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>The numbers are minus twenty and twenty three, which make three. The sum is minus seven f minus four s plus three.

beats.on_screen: Step 5 (e) and (f): the second expression is the first with every sign changed ; each term cancels ; sum 0

marks.s5a: the signs of the first expression are compared with the second
marks.s5b: each term cancels with its opposite and 0 is written twice

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Fifth, look at the last two pairs. In each pair, the second expression is the first one with every sign changed.
<bookmark mark='s5b'/>Every term cancels with its opposite, so each sum is zero.

marks.s6a: 1 replaces d and c in the first pair

narration: <bookmark mark='s6a'/>Sixth, check the first pair with d as one and c as one.
<bookmark mark='s6b'/>The first expression gives four minus seven plus nine, which is six. The second gives eight minus eleven plus nine, which is also six.
<bookmark mark='s6c'/>Their sum is twelve. Thirteen plus one minus two is twelve as well.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Every pair has now been added.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>The sums are thirteen d plus c minus two, and seven f plus four s minus four.
<bookmark mark='ans3'/>Next are two c minus d minus two, and minus seven f minus four s plus three.
<bookmark mark='ans4'/>The last two sums are both zero.
